standard_prerequisites.name: An elementary etale neighbourhood on which the module has projective global sections, and purity of an affine locally projective module
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, labels lemma-finite-presentation-flat-along-fibre (proof line 5422) and lemma-affine-locally-projective-pure (proof line 5436)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the affine etale neighbourhood S_i' -> S_i and the etale X_i' -> X_i whose global sections of the pulled back module are projective over the base, and gives that this pulled back module is universally pure over S_i'.

standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion for purity through associated primes and constructibility of the relative assassin condition
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, labels lemma-criterion (proof lines 5452 and 5484); More on Morphisms, labels more-morphisms-lemma-relative-assassin-constructible (proof line 5461) and more-morphisms-lemma-base-change-assassin-in-U (proof line 5471); Limits, label limits-lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible (proof line 5482)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns purity along the fibre into an inclusion of the relative associated primes inside the image of the etale morphism, makes the two sets of points where that inclusion holds locally constructible and compatible with base change, and allows the inclusion to be tested at a finite stage because the local ring of the limit is the filtered colimit of the local rings of the stages.

core_obligations: Descend the data to a stage: let U be the open flat locus of F over S, which is open by the openness of flatness theorem, and choose a quasi-compact open U' of U containing the quasi-compact fibre X_s; then descend the morphism, the module, the open U' and the flatness of the module on U' to some stage i, so that F_i is flat along (X_i)_{s_i} (proof lines 5394-5418).

Choose an affine etale neighbourhood trivialising the module: apply the flat along the fibre lemma to get an elementary etale neighbourhood (S_i', s_i') and an etale g_i : X_i' -> X_i covering (X_i)_{s_i} with X_i' and S_i' affine and with the global sections of the pulled back module projective over the base, and note that the pulled back module is universally pure over S_i' by the affine locally projective purity lemma; base change this set-up both to later stages and to the limit (proof lines 5420-5441).

Transfer purity to a finite stage: let W'_i be the image of the etale morphism, form W'_{i'} and W' by base change, use the purity of F along X_s and the criterion to get the inclusion of the relative associated primes of F over S' inside W', observe via constructibility of the relative assassin condition that the corresponding sets E, E_i and E_{i'} are locally constructible and compatible with base change, and conclude with the colimit description of the local ring O_{S',s'} that Spec(O_{S'_{i'}, s'_{i'}}) lands in E_i for some i'; applying the criterion once more over S_{i'} gives that F_{i'} is pure along (X_{i'})_{s_{i'}} (proof lines 5443-5486).
proof_roadmap: Use openness of flatness and the descent lemmas to move the whole situation to a stage of the inverse system (proof lines 5394-5418).
Build the affine etale neighbourhood on which the module has projective global sections (proof lines 5420-5441).

Express purity through the relative associated primes, make the condition constructible and base change compatible, and read it off at a finite stage by the colimit description of the local ring (proof lines 5443-5486).
difficulty_reason: The lemma descends a finite presentation morphism together with a finitely presented module that is pure along a fibre and flat over the base at every point of that fibre: after possibly moving along the directed system there is a stage carrying a morphism and a module with the same properties whose base change is the given pair (statement lines 5377-5392, tag 05MA). The proof is a real limit argument: it descends the flat locus and its quasi-compact piece, builds an affine etale neighbourhood over a stage on which the module has projective global sections, rewrites purity as an inclusion of the relative associated primes, uses constructibility and base change compatibility of that inclusion so that it can be tested at a finite stage through the colimit description of the local ring at the limit, and then applies the purity criterion over that stage. The constructibility step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
